restaurant-at-amar-khamar.blurb: Amar Khamar Lunch Room at 21B Hindustan Road: an intimate dining room built around seasonal, home-style Bengali cooking.

tips.expect: Seasonal Bengali food sourced from farming communities across Bengal, served in a calm, home-like room. Both fish and meat dishes and vegetarian options are on offer.
tips.good: The Chhuti-r Bhat, a long tasting meal that respects the traditional order of eating.
tips.watch: Reported open Tuesday to Sunday, 12:30 to 10 pm, and closed on Mondays. A full tasting meal takes a while, so don't squeeze it in between pandals.
tips.tip: Go for a slow Puja lunch rather than a rush dinner. It is a short walk from Hindustan Park.

yokocho.blurb: Calcutta's first East-inspired bar and BBQ, on the first floor of Park Centre on Park Street. The menu draws on Japan, Thailand, Vietnam and Singapore.

tips.expect: Alley-dining style Eastern plates and a cocktail programme inspired by informal Japanese drinking culture, from chef Auroni Mookerjee's kitchen.
tips.good: The playful take on local flavours, such as the temaki tacos inspired by prawn cocktail.
tips.watch: It is on the first floor of a commercial building, so the entrance is easy to miss from the street.
tips.tip: A good late-evening stop after Park Street pandal-hopping.

rever-glasshouse-cafe.blurb: A two-floor glasshouse cafe on Lake Road that opened in 2024, mixing old-Calcutta charm with a modern look.
dishes: Shisha and live music in select hours

tips.expect: A large, elegant glass-fronted space with around 120 covers and a global fusion menu.
tips.good: The cold brews and the setting. It is a pleasant place to sit between pandals.
tips.watch: Prices at other outlets are about ₹1,200 for two. Live-music hours are limited.
tips.tip: It sits in the Lake Road cafe cluster, so there are several options within a few minutes if it's full.

eau-chew.blurb: A family-run eating house on Ganesh Chandra Avenue, founded by a Chinese immigrant. It is described as one of the oldest Chinese restaurants in Kolkata, running for 90+ years.

tips.expect: Old-Calcutta Chinese food from family recipes, in a no-frills room.
tips.good: The slow-cooked chimney soup (made in a coal-burning vessel) and the generous portions.
tips.watch: A traditional place that is not about aesthetics. Pork is on the menu, so check if that matters to you.
tips.tip: Combine it with Chinatown and New Market, then walk on to Park Street.

conversation-room.blurb: A cocktail bar at 1 Edward Court on Chowringhee Road, with old-world decor, weathered walls and a cosy mood.
dishes: The Eavesdropper (tequila, Cointreau, cranberry, Schezwan sauce)

tips.expect: Inventive cocktails and small and big plates with an international twist.
tips.good: The cocktail craft and the unusual food pairings. A strong choice for a date night.
tips.watch: It is a bar first. Puja Saturdays and Sundays will be busy.
tips.tip: Reserve if you can, and note that it is on Chowringhee, far from the North Kolkata circuit.

siuli-the-parcel-cafe.blurb: India's first post-office cafe, inside the historic General Post Office at BBD Bagh.

tips.expect: A small cafe with colourful wooden furniture and sofas for about 34 people, inside a colonial building. You can also get parcels packed and buy post-office souvenirs.
tips.good: The setting is the point: coffee under the GPO's arches, away from the crowds.
tips.watch: When it launched it was open 10 am to 7 pm and closed Sundays. Saptami falls on a Sunday this year, so check before you go.
tips.tip: A great weekday morning stop before BBD Bagh and Esplanade sightseeing.

glenburn-cafe.blurb: A Park Street tea room at 7A Russel Street serving the Glenburn estate's own Darjeeling, Assam and flavoured teas.

tips.expect: A calm tearoom with small plates and tapas, a break from the Park Street bustle. About ₹800 to ₹1,000 for two.
tips.good: The tea list. It is a rare place to try estate teas properly.
tips.watch: Reported hours are 9 am to 9 pm, so it is not a late-night option.
tips.tip: Good for a mid-afternoon reset between Park Street and Esplanade.

pico-pizzeria-and-coffee-bar.blurb: A pizzeria and coffee bar on Lake Road near Southern Avenue, known for wood-fired pizzas and good coffee.

tips.expect: A cosy, welcoming room with friendly service. About ₹1,000 for two.
tips.good: The wood-fired char on the pizzas, and the coffee.
tips.watch: Seats go quickly on weekend evenings in the Lake Road and Southern Avenue area.
tips.tip: Combine it with Hindustan Park pandals nearby.

cafe-de-rois.blurb: A Parisian-style cafe on Paddapukur Road, Bhowanipore, with chic European decor.

tips.expect: A stylish cafe with an all-day menu of pizza, pasta, Continental, Chinese, desserts and coffee. About ₹1,500 for two.
tips.good: The decor, and a menu broad enough for a mixed group.
tips.watch: It also screens live sports, which can make evenings noisy.
tips.tip: Handy near the Bhowanipore Mallick Bari.

bageecha-cafe.blurb: A garden-inspired vegetarian cafe by the Ganga, on the Polo Floatel at BBD Bagh. It has three zones: Ghar, Verandah and Terrace.

tips.expect: A calm riverside garden vibe with vintage indoor seating, a breezy verandah overlooking the river and a terrace under a gulmohar tree. About ₹800 and up for two.
tips.good: The Ganga view and the all-vegetarian menu, which is unusual for the area.
tips.watch: Open about 11 am to 11 pm. Weekends and evenings fill up for the sunset.
tips.tip: Time it for golden hour, then walk to Esplanade or catch the Strand Road lights.

colab-coffee-calcutta.blurb: A specialty coffee cafe at Jodhpur Gardens, Lake Gardens, known for Naples-style pizza and good coffee.

tips.expect: An aesthetic cafe with higher prices than a typical coffee shop. About ₹1,200 for two.
tips.good: Quality of coffee and food in a stylish room.
tips.watch: Reported open daily 10 am to 10 pm. Pricey for a casual coffee.
tips.tip: There is another CōLAB at Deshapriya Park, right on the Kalighat pandal route.

milloh-caf-sector-v.blurb: A Sector V cafe known for playful Indian-fusion plates, open from about noon to 11 pm.

tips.expect: Creative street-food-inspired plates in an easy cafe setting, with outdoor seating. About ₹1,000 for two.
tips.good: The Indian-fusion small plates. It is kid-friendly and wheelchair accessible.
tips.watch: There is also a newer vegetarian Milloh on Sarat Bose Road, so check which outlet you mean.
tips.tip: A good stop after Salt Lake pandals, close to Sector V metro.
